about.title: One clinic, two kinds of care, no runaround
body: London Dental and Health Center was started with a simple idea: a neighborhood in Senneerkuppam and Kattupakkam shouldn't need to travel across the city for routine dental work or a general check-up. Both live here, in the same clinic, on Christ School Road.

Whether it's a child's first dental visit, a root canal that's been put off too long, or a fever that needs a doctor's eye before it gets worse, our team treats every visit the same way — unhurried, explained clearly, and priced honestly before any treatment begins.
highlights: Dental and general medicine under one roof

services.name: General Health Consultation
services.overview: From fevers and infections to ongoing conditions like diabetes and hypertension, our general physician provides thorough consultations with clear next steps, not just a prescription.

Physical examination
Lab tests referral if needed

Clear explanation of diagnosis and treatment

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before a consultation?
faqs.answer: Not for a general consultation. If blood tests are recommended, we'll let you know if fasting is required beforehand.

faqs.question: Can I get a prescription refill without a full visit?
faqs.answer: For existing patients on ongoing medication, a brief follow-up visit is usually enough — call ahead and we'll fit you in.

services.name: Dental Checkup & Treatment
services.tagline: Routine exams, cleaning, and general dental care
services.overview: Regular dental checkups catch problems while they're still small. We combine thorough exams with cleaning, fillings, and general treatment in a single, unhurried visit.
procedure: Oral examination and X-ray if needed
Scaling and cleaning
Filling or minor treatment as required
Home care guidance
benefits: Early detection of cavities and gum issues
Same-visit treatment for most routine cases
services.recovery: No downtime for checkups and cleaning; minor treatments allow you to return to normal eating within a few hours.

faqs.question: How often should I get a dental checkup?
faqs.answer: We recommend every six months for most patients, though your dentist may suggest more frequent visits if you have ongoing issues.

services.name: Root Canal Treatment
services.tagline: Save the tooth, stop the pain
services.overview: When decay or infection reaches the tooth's nerve, root canal treatment removes the source of pain and preserves the natural tooth instead of extracting it.
symptoms: Sensitivity to hot or cold that lingers
Swelling or a pimple-like bump on the gum
procedure: Diagnosis with clinical exam and X-ray
Local anesthesia and cleaning of the root canal
Sealing the canal
Crown placement to protect the treated tooth
benefits: Relieves pain at the source, not just symptoms
Completed across one to two visits in most cases
services.recovery: Mild soreness for a day or two is normal; most patients return to normal eating within 24–48 hours.

faqs.question: Is root canal treatment painful?
faqs.answer: The procedure itself is done under local anesthesia and is generally no more uncomfortable than a filling. Some soreness afterward is normal and manageable with medication.

faqs.question: How many visits does it take?
faqs.answer: Most root canals are completed in one to two visits, depending on the tooth and extent of infection.

services.name: Minor Procedures
services.tagline: Extractions, wound care, and small surgical needs
services.overview: For tooth extractions, minor wound dressing, and small in-clinic procedures, our team handles the work with proper sterilization and clear aftercare instructions.
symptoms: Minor cuts or wounds needing dressing
Ingrown nail or minor skin concerns
procedure: Assessment and consent discussion
Local anesthesia where applicable
Procedure performed under sterile conditions
Aftercare instructions and follow-up if needed
benefits: Avoid a hospital visit for minor, routine procedures
Clear aftercare guidance to prevent complications
services.recovery: Recovery depends on the procedure — most minor extractions and dressings heal within a few days with basic care.

faqs.question: Do you accept walk-in patients?
faqs.answer: Yes, walk-ins are welcome for both dental and general consultations, though booking an appointment ahead of time helps avoid waiting.

faqs.question: What services are available at the clinic?
faqs.answer: We offer general health consultations, dental checkups and treatment, root canal treatment, minor procedures, and preventive health checkup packages, all at one location.

faqs.question: What should I expect on my first visit?
faqs.answer: Your first visit includes a review of your medical or dental history, an examination, and a clear explanation of any recommended treatment before we proceed.

faqs.question: What payment methods do you accept?
faqs.answer: We accept cash, UPI, and major debit and credit cards. Pricing for any treatment is shared upfront before you commit to it.

blogPosts.title: Why Your Family Needs Both a Dentist and a Doctor Nearby
blogPosts.excerpt: Dental health and general health affect each other more than most people realize — here's why keeping both close matters.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Priya Natarajan
content: It's easy to think of dental care and general health as separate categories — one for your teeth, one for everything else. In practice, they overlap constantly. Gum infections have been linked to heart health, uncontrolled diabetes shows up first in the mouth as slow-healing gums, and a child running a fever is sometimes actually dealing with a dental abscess, not a viral infection.

When a dentist and a general physician work in the same clinic, that overlap stops being a coordination problem. A patient who comes in for a toothache but mentions they've also been unusually tired can be seen by both of us in the same visit, instead of being sent across town with a referral slip and told to come back another day.

This matters even more for families with young children and elderly parents. Kids need dental visits that don't turn into an ordeal, and older patients often manage multiple conditions where a small dental issue can complicate things like blood sugar control. Having both kinds of care under one roof means fewer visits, fewer missed follow-ups, and a care team that actually has the full picture.

Practically speaking, we'd encourage every family to have a routine: a dental checkup every six months, and a general health checkup at least once a year, ideally at a clinic close enough that neither one feels like a chore. That's the entire reason London Dental and Health Center exists on Christ School Road — so that routine is actually easy to keep.
